diagnostics.notes: Claim extractions match their sources. A: RCT in smokers using varenicline, low-carbohydrate vs moderately fat-reduced diet, weight change at 12 weeks, explicit conclusion of no difference ('no better than a fat-reduced diet'). B: network meta-analysis, low-carbohydrate vs standard hypolipemic diet, significant weight reduction (MD -6.31 kg). Comparators are sufficiently similar (fat-reduced/low-fat), outcome is weight change in both. Per decision order, A's explicit no-difference conclusion against B's reported effect takes the not_replicated branch; population/context differences (smoking-cessation with varenicline vs general overweight/obese weight-loss trials) are noted but not needed for the branch.

source_evidence.quote: In overweight or obese smokers using varenicline a low-carbohydrate diet was no better than a fat-reduced diet in reducing weight gain

both the low-carbohydrate diet (MD = -6.31 kg, 95% CI: -11.23, -1.39) and the low-fat diet (MD = -5.61 kg, 95% CI: -10.61, -0.61) significantly reduced weight among overweight/obese adults compared to the standard hypolipemic diet

verdict.label: not_replicated
verdict.rationale: Both findings concern low-carbohydrate diets and weight change against a fat-reduced/low-fat comparator in overweight/obese adults, so they are comparable. Study A (RCT, PMID 26242289) explicitly concludes no difference: 'a low-carbohydrate diet was no better than a fat-reduced diet in reducing weight gain' (12-week weight change -0.2 vs 0.5 kg, not statistically significant). Study B (network meta-analysis, PMID 39255914) reports the low-carbohydrate diet significantly reduced weight versus a standard hypolipemic diet (MD -6.31 kg, 95% CI -11.23, -1.39). An explicit no-difference conclusion against a reported effect takes the not_replicated branch; the differing contexts (smokers quitting with varenicline vs general overweight/obese weight-loss trials) are contextual notes, not the basis of the label.
